text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers.

- Austria's population will have gone down so much by the year 2020 that foreign workers will have to be brought into the country, according to a study by the Institute for System Analysis. The percentage of pensioners will rise to over 30 percent from about 20 percent currently, meaning fewer employees will have to carry the pension burden.
- The stock exchange may become a company with shareholders. A decision over the future of the exchange, futures and options exchange OeTOB and the Control Bank could come in November.

- Chancellor Franz Vranitzky, on a visit to Beijing with an Austrian business delegation, says China is accepting a dialogue on human rights issues. He is also optimistic that Austria will achieve export projects worth billions of schillings.
- Unions are demanding two free Saturdays a month for shop workers before they agree to liberalised shopping hours. The Chamber of Economy opposes the union stance.
- The Social Democrats have above 40 percent backing, according to the latest surveys ahead of Sunday's Vienna state elections. The far-right Freedom Party has the support of a quarter of Viennese.
- Work at German tyre maker Continental's Austrian unit Semperit might be guaranteed for the next two years under specific rules.
- Austrian car subcontractor Miba should achieve its planned turnover of 2.4 billion schillings. However, chief executive Peter Mitterbauer sees troubles in Italy next year.
- Austria's social partnership should be reformed, Peter Mitterbauer, president of the Industrialists' Association said.
- Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation is rumoured to be considering a consortium bid for Austria's third mobile telephone licence.
